headline: Right to Repair obligations bite importers as Green Claims Directive wavers
summary: EU Right to Repair rules now place direct compliance duties on finished-goods importers. Meanwhile, reports indicate the European Commission has dropped the proposed Green Claims Directive, though general anti-greenwashing rules remain relevant for product marketing.

items.title: EU Right to Repair rules place obligations on importers
items.what: New Right to Repair legislation has taken effect, while the EU Commission opened a consultation on further strengthening product repairability requirements.
items.meaning: As an importer selling under your own brand, you hold primary responsibility for providing repair access, spare parts, and documentation for consumer equipment.
items.action: Audit repair manuals and spare parts supply chains with your Chinese manufacturing partners.

sources.title: New Law on Right to Repair Takes Effect
EU Right-to-Repair Rules Put Importers And Distributors On The Hook
EU launches consultation on tougher repairability rules to cut waste

items.title: EU Commission reportedly abandons proposed Green Claims Directive
items.what: Reports state the European Commission has dropped the proposed Green Claims Directive, abandoning plans for mandatory independent pre-verification of environmental claims.
items.meaning: Substantiation obligations may be less rigid without ex-ante verification, but product sustainability claims remain subject to EU consumer protection rules.
items.action: Continue collecting verifiable sustainability data from suppliers to support brand claims.

sources.title: EU Commission Scraps Green Claims Directive
Independent verification for greenwashing claims officially dropped by EU Commission
EU policy arm calls to kill-off 'in-limbo' Green Claims Directive

items.title: ESPR increases focus on stock write-offs and circular returns
items.what: Industry reports highlight high write-off rates for returned stock as Ecodesign rules push companies towards circular business models and waste reduction.
items.meaning: Returned power tools and battery packs face growing scrutiny regarding refurbishment and waste prevention across EU distribution networks.
items.action: Review product return policies and reverse logistics arrangements with retail partners.

sources.title: Half of retailers write off up to 40 per cent of returned stock, as ESPR raises pressure on circular returns
